answer: Latency-Bound Identity Claiming. Each new agent identity must complete a challenge-response round trip to a randomly assigned physical island relay, timed so the reply can only arrive after the true propagation delay from that site. A falcon does not help here: the operator cannot compress physics. Because one machine cannot occupy two distant relays at once, each identity carries a real per-claim cost of dedicated hardware, a leased line, and geographic presence. The whisper of a spoofed timestamp is detectable against measured round-trip bounds.
